- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) or shows strong negative swings, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk-off bias.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment was bullish; cap forecast at 1-2% above peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to correct; add 0.5-1.0% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; smooth out forecast by averaging last 5-7 days’ trend.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast with sentiment’s recent 3-day average.
